replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation: To both parties. The record settles this case on the route-deviation test, and the answer is that the charge stands. The booking was Blk 118 Rivervale Drive to Changi Terminal 1, but the endpoints were changed twice after booking: the rider moved the pickup pin to Punggol MRT at 07:12:30, and at 07:41:52 the dropoff was changed to Terminal 3 — both are recorded on the trip record (pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at) and both are confirmed by the four-message chat log. POL-RD-05 therefore requires the distance comparison to be re-run against the platform's stored re-quote between the AMENDED endpoints, 24.60 km (amended_optimal_distance_km), with 31.0 minutes as its duration — not against the original 21.0 km booking estimate. On that baseline the governing figure is the trace distance of 26.17 km: POL-RD-01 directs the tribunal to gps_trace.trace_distance_km and forbids citing the rounded 26.2 km copy carried on the trip record and the fare breakdown. Excess is 26.17 − 24.60 = 1.57 km, or 6.4% of the amended optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 0.8 km absolute and 20% of the optimal; 6.4% fails the proportional limb, so no deviation is established, and POL-RD-05 states that where no deviation survives the recomputation the outcome is NO_ACTION. The rider's 5.17 km / 24.62% figure, and the trip record's 24.8% deviation_pct, are both measured against the 21.0 km booking estimate that the amendments displaced; they do not answer the amended-baseline question. The driver is not required to invoke any exculpatory clause, and the absence of a traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0) changes nothing either way. The rider's arithmetic under POL-RD-02 (a recomputed fare of 27.63 and a 6.15 refund) is correct as arithmetic but only runs once a deviation is established against the correct baseline; it is not, so no distance-or-time refund is due. The rider's point that POL-RD-05 also licenses PARTIAL_REFUND does not help: the residue she points to cannot clear the POL-RD-01 gate, and the clause's own text returns NO_ACTION where no deviation survives. As to the 'five minutes driving around the airport', that is the Terminal 3 kerb loop that followed her own change of destination — the chat log records the request at 07:41:40 and the amendment at 07:41:52, and the trace shows two loops of the T3 departure kerb inside 380 m of the amended pin. POL-RD-05 excludes circling near an amended point where the rider is not present, and in any event the whole excess on the amended baseline is only 1.57 km, far short of the threshold, so no refund turns on it. The billing-integrity check finds no defect: the fare reconciles to the cent (3.80 base + 19.65 distance + 9.52 time + 0.80 platform fee = 33.77), with no ERP lines, no surge, no waiting fee and no promo discount, and the airport surcharge is correctly 0.00 because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there — so no standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4) arises. No conduct referral arises either: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 402, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06, and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4 that would engage the extra-corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08. Profile fields were used only for the tests that name them. The fare stands as charged, and NO_ACTION leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are. Trace integrity was checked and is clean: 206 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so POL-RD-07 does not bite and no escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires.
